name: Europe hybrid attacks
summary: Hoax bomb threats disrupt at least 27 European flights on 5 Nov; no state blamed
state: Emailed bomb threats disrupted at least 27 passenger flights across ten European countries on 5 Nov, the second wave that week; French jets escorted an Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight to Évreux and Bulgaria escorted three airliners (Al Jazeera). No explosives were found and no government has named a culprit; the EU said it was too early to say whether the alerts were linked (Skift).
for_you: Expect occasional diversions and security checks on European flights; follow airline and airport instructions.
rubric_hit: Wave of disruptive incidents in Europe, not yet attributed to a state = Watch (kept)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — New bomb threats force more European flights into emergency landings

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
